title: Recover an extreme channel complement from the whole finite mixed bath
status_authority: Actual supplied source passages and scoped internal audits; no new Capital science verification.
reported_status: Separate companion theorem reported by the source: for an exact EXTREME CPTP channel with an initially uncorrelated finite mixed bath, the whole physical bath output has B(rho)=W[C(rho) tensor tau]W^dagger. Local CPTP output processing therefore recovers the complete minimal complement without the bath purifier. The normal form forces r rank(tau)<=dim E_out and certifies, rather than creates, pure virtual resources. Given actual B and a right inverse of C, a positively regularized whole-bath decoder has exact success at least 1-D lambda and deterministic error at most 2D lambda. A conditioned near-target robustness claim and an amplitude-damping dual-rail use are also reported. This whole-bath decoder is NOT automatically causal, no thermal-input causal reception is proved, and ambiguous DOM coefficients are not reconstructed.

proof_availability.classification_scope: The companion result requires the exact extreme-channel, uncorrelated-initial-bath and whole-output premises. It neither turns an arbitrary thermal bath into a pure resource nor makes every extreme channel's complement quantum-capable. In the stated fixed finite bath/equal source-dimension setting, a nonunitary extreme implementation requires an appropriate pure virtual subsystem; this certifies rather than creates purity. Near-target robustness depends on the fixed target and its right inverse. A bath-dimension-independent analytic error bound does not make full bath acquisition or synthesis cheap. The native prefix stops during the argument and the DOM ending breaks/duplicates mathematical glyphs; ambiguous nested-radical coefficients are not reconstructed. Original report/code/audits remain unacquired, with no new Capital/root audit or hardware/priority claim.
